screen1-a3.convention_relied_on: the Facebook 'f' logo = open Facebook - my reading; it is a brand mark rather than a generic action glyph
screen1-a3.initial_rationale: no visible word; the glyph is the Facebook brand mark, which a first-time user widely reads as 'go to Facebook'; exemption pending a tap

screen1-a5.description: control showing 'Ask Meta AI or search'
screen1-a5.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc 'Ask Meta AI or search' - read only to know what to test for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a5.initial_rationale: the only text is the placeholder 'Ask Meta AI or search', which names two different jobs in one field and does not say what is searched; it is gone once typing starts

test_cases.confirms_if: the placeholder gives no hint and results are unrelated
test_cases.overturns_if: matching people are listed and the field still shows what it is for
test_cases.observed_result: the placeholder disappeared on the first letter; results showed 'Deki - Connected' and a 'More people' list; an 'Ask' chip appeared inside the field

test_cases.action: type the literal text 'what is the weather today' (the 'Ask Meta AI' reading)
test_cases.expected_result: Meta AI answers, or the field makes clear the question goes to Meta AI
test_cases.confirms_if: a question is handled as a plain search with no answer
test_cases.overturns_if: the question is routed to Meta AI
test_cases.observed_result: no answer appeared; the list showed 'More people' accounts with names like 'What is the weather for today in san fernando'; only the small 'Ask' chip in the field pointed to Meta AI

screen1-a5.deciding_evidence: a typed question was treated as a people search (accounts whose names resemble the words); reaching Meta AI needs a separate 'Ask' chip that only appears after typing, and the placeholder vanished on the first keystroke
screen1-a5.recommendation: give the field a persistent label such as 'Search people and chats' and a separate, always-visible 'Ask Meta AI' button, instead of one placeholder naming both jobs

screen1-a6.accessibility_text_consulted: content_desc 'Your note' - read only to know what to test for; not used in the verdict
screen1-a6.initial_rationale: the bubble shows a prompt phrase ('Drop a thought' / 'What's up?') - an idiom that does not say it posts a public note, or for how long

test_cases.action: tap the speech bubble above the 'You' tile
test_cases.expected_result: a place to write a short status opens
test_cases.confirms_if: it opens something the phrase does not predict (a public post) without saying so
test_cases.overturns_if: the destination matches what the phrase suggests
test_cases.observed_result: a 'New note' composer opened with 'Share a thought...' and the footer 'Anyone can see your note on Messenger and Facebook for 24 hours. Change'; the bubble's own wording changed between visits ('Drop a thought', 'Share a song', 'Post a note...')

screen1-a6.deciding_evidence: the bubble opened a 'New note' composer whose footer says 'Anyone can see your note on Messenger and Facebook for 24 hours' - nothing on the bubble said it creates a public post
screen1-a6.recommendation: label the bubble 'Post a note' and say who sees it (e.g. 'Post a note - visible for 24 h')
